look_here_first: Check growth habit and the structures immediately below the calyx. Winecup is a perennial with low trailing/decumbent stems and an involucel of 3 bractlets beneath the flower. The calyx lobes are already divergent in bud rather than meeting to form a pointed bud.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: stems decumbent/trailing to weakly erect, generally much lower than tall poppymallow

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves alternate, roundish in outline and deeply 3–5(–7)-lobed

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: foliage hairy with stellate and simple hairs

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: three involucellar/epicalyx bractlets immediately below calyx

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calyx lobes divergent in bud, not forming an apiculate point

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowers cup-shaped; petal color variable and secondary for ID

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: schizocarp with 10–28 indehiscent mericarps; beaks not strongly prominent

lookalikes.differences: Callirhoe leiocarpa: C. leiocarpa is annual/biennial and tall/erect, lacks involucellar bractlets, has calyx lobes meeting into a pointed bud, and has glabrous dehiscent mericarps with prominent beaks. Callirhoe pedata: C. pedata is an erect/ascending perennial and lacks the low trailing winecup habit; fruit and leaf architecture should be checked when flowers are absent. Callirhoe scabriuscula: Texas poppy-mallow is stiffly erect, densely stellate-hairy and taller; winecup is low/trailing and has different hair/habit characters.
